text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Retail currency shops trade the leu currency at a rate 35 percent lower than that of the interbank market.
- While Romania faces tight foreign exchange constraints, exporters failed to repatriate more than $8.5 million.
TINERETUL LIBER
- U.S. food giant McDonald's opened a fast-food restaurant in Ploiesti.
LIBERTATEA
- Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu's cabinet issued a 23-page booklet outlining the achievements of four years in office.
- The nascent over-the-counter market now trades 30 stocks.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Primary school children in Bucharest had to complete a form outlining their parents' "political affiliation" and dates from the identity cards, which the newspaper describes as a throwback to the communist era and might be used for fraud in Sunday's presidential run-off.
- The newspaper publishes the list of the new elected members of both parliament houses in the November 3 elections.
- Under the headline "His power is a diversion", the newspaper publishes an editorial on incumbent President Ion Iliescu's latest statements against his rival ahead of the presidential run-off.

- "Iliescu don't forget, Transylvanian does not want you," shouted several thousand people at the end of Iliescu's electoral rally in Alba Iulia. The newspaper says that busses with miners were brought to support Iliescu.
- The Community of Ethnic Gyspies in Romania backs Constantinescu due to "Romania's economic and social crises which has to change radically and without delays."
ADEVARUL
- An editorial on the President Iliescu's campaign clip denounces its "aggressive" and "Bolshevik" nature alleging that Iliescu "is below (former dictator Nicolae) Ceausescu."
- U.S. Congresmen deny that the American government is implicated in President Iliescu's electoral campaign.
- Tudor Mohora, head of the Socialist Party (PS), says he will support Emil Constantinescu as the party's aspirations are not reflected in President Iliescu's programme.
- The Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) supports Emil Constantinescu who "represents the political change expected by whole Romania."
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Constantinescu says in an appeal to the miners that "the time of hate has past" asking for their support in the run-off.
- The Democratic Convention and Social Democratic Union, allied to back Constantinescu in the second round run-off, hold a campaign rally in Bucharest on Wednesday.
- The newspaper says that no party other than the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) is backing President Iliescu in the second round of the presidential elections.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The newspaper publishes excerpts from President Iliescu's speech at the rally in Alba Iulia where he said "I'd prefer to lose rather than give into pressure which could endanger Romaniar", a reference to alleged claims to autonomy by the Hungarian minority.
- Romania's Orthodox Patriarch Teoctist celebrated 10 years since he was appointed.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- The newspaper publishes a full-page of statements from farmers from a southern village saying why they back Iliescu.
DIMINEATA

- "By voting Emil (Constantinescu) you vote for (ex-King) Michael" reads a headline on the alleged intention of the CDR candidate to overturn the constitutional order and bring former King Michael to Romania. ($=3,450 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
